coaching.headline: Objectives decided this one: five of six majors went our way, and five of six won fights were cashed into a prize.

flags.text: Khaimera ran the damn objectives: 45765 objective damage, most of all ten, and four of our five majors.
Primal Fangtooth fight won 4-1, then both inner towers, both inhibitors and Steel's final hit on the Core.
Shit timing around the second Mini Prime: Murdock died just before, Khaimera and Ikra just after.
Murdock's eight deaths included three outside any detected fight, to Argus, Sparrow and The Fey.

focus.title: Cash every fight, lose no bodies at the pit
focus.action: Keep turning each won fight into the nearest tower or major. Around a Mini Prime or Fangtooth, Murdock and Ikra stay grouped with Steel and Khaimera before and after the take.

19.7.call: Lost 2-4 in two separate plays: Khaimera and Ikra fell in our jungle, Serath killed Murdock and Steel on the duo lane. With two down after a Mini Prime, reset before contesting again.

27.8.call: Two picks in two separate plays shortly after Ikra's death: Khaimera killed Serath on the duo lane, Murdock killed Riktor on the offlane, then the enemy offlane outer fell. Repeat the push after every pick.

29.7.call: The Fey killed Murdock first, yet Khaimera still secured Primal Fangtooth and the fight finished 4-1. When the carry drops first, secure the objective, then fight.

5465c135-0f7c-423a-9fe6-8272d7d92356: Five deaths on the duo lane in our half, three to Sparrow and two to Argus. When Steel roams, farm near our tower instead of trading.
Team-high 31647 hero damage, but 4.9 CS per minute against a 6.2 norm. Between fights, clear the duo wave before roaming.
cf65b5c7-d458-4076-b712-271b5289b778: Four kills on other lanes before the enemy mid outer fell; the first, on Riktor, came shortly before our first Mini Prime. Keep rotating once the mid wave is pushed.
Most gold of all ten, 17843, and razed the enemy mid outer, yet two deaths came outside any detected fight. Late on the duo lane, move with Khaimera.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Secured the first Fangtooth and led all ten with 20037 healing while absorbing 58591 damage for two deaths. In grouped fights, stand in front of Murdock and Ikra.
Hit hard: 771 hero damage per minute against a 561 norm, yet Riktor razed our offlane outer early. When Riktor rotates away, push the offlane tower.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Ran the frontline: 67333 mitigated, most of all ten, 58% kill participation and the Core's final hit. Next objective, open with Shield Slam with all five up.
Ten wards and three cleared against 24 from Argus; enemy vision ran 52 to our 35. Before each Mini Prime, clear and ward the Prime pit approach.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Eleven kills, the most of all ten, from first blood on Riktor to kills on The Fey and Sparrow in the closing fight. After Shield Slam lands, follow with Cull.
Three wards against a 4.7 norm; the death to Sparrow at the Fangtooth pit came just before the enemy took Fangtooth. Ward or sweep that pit before contesting.

matchup: Murdock and Sparrow traded kills three for three, and Murdock killed Argus three times against two deaths to Argus.
Argus's Dread Nova stuns in a small area; The Fey's Fly Trap pulls attached heroes inward, then stuns.
build: Vanquisher is the one item shared with the most played core into Sparrow; Lightning Hawk and Imperator are missing.
Vanquisher executes heroes taken below a small health threshold.
Demolisher, finished last, ignores a share of physical armor; earlier fights ran without Demolisher.
eternal: Demiurge boosts stats from items and item-effect damage; Bloatware adds damage and damage reduction per item.
Thraex leans first in the Murdock carry field; Demiurge has too few games to lead.
Construct with Bloatware is the best Demiurge pair; Tri-Core with Bloatware is the most played.
augment: Sting Operation adds Static Trap charges and makes the traps larger.
Justice's Reach is clearly the best Murdock carry augment; Sting Operation ranks second.
crest: Eviscerator's active adds attack speed, omnivamp and empowered on-hit basic attacks for a short window.
Pacifier is clearly the best Murdock carry crest; Eviscerator ranks behind.
improvement: Sparrow wins this lane 53% of the time and no physical armor was built; Sparrow's damage was almost all physical.
Justice's Reach over Sting Operation is the field-backed swap: Shots Fired pierces units with more range, giving up extra traps.
Pacifier over Eviscerator stays on the Sharpshooter Crest path: a dash and an empowered physical hit instead of the attack-speed window.

matchup: Lane opponent was The Fey: one Ikra kill on The Fey, two Ikra deaths to The Fey, both in our half.
Serath's Heaven's Fury grants CC immunity and invulnerability, so Narcosis cannot stop that dash.
build: Overseer is the one core item built; Combustion and Wraith Leggings are missing.
Overseer makes the ultimate hit harder and heals Ikra from ultimate damage on heroes; Overseer was finished last.
Megacosm adds damage over time from ability hits, scaled by the target's max and bonus health.
eternal: Aion grants mana regeneration on casts and gold from spell damage on heroes; Runic Focus turns current mana into magical power.
Demiurge leans first in the Ikra mid field, Aion behind Vesh; Bottomless Vial with Runic Focus is the best Aion pair.
augment: Cascade builds stacks on Fathom hits toward a bonus Brine hit and grants attack speed on ability damage.
The Gloom leans first in the Ikra mid augment field; Cascade ranks third, behind Undertow.
crest: Epoch's active puts Ikra in stasis briefly.
Epoch leans first in the Ikra mid crest field. Sound keep.
improvement: The Fey wins this lane 54.1% of the time and no magical armor was built against The Fey's magical damage.
The Gloom over Cascade is the field lean: Bubbles grow and camouflage Ikra and allies inside, giving up the attack-speed stacks.
Demiurge over Aion is the field lean: item stat and item-effect boosts instead of mana and spell gold.

matchup: Lane opponent was Riktor: both Greystone deaths went to Riktor, and Greystone never killed Riktor.
Riktor's Skewer suppresses, Riplash pulls heroes in, and Shock Therapy silences and destroys shields, including the Forticus shield.
build: Overlord, Rapture and Aegis Of Agawar are the full winning core.
Forticus adds armor, tenacity and a shield upon taking hero damage.
Aegis Of Agawar and Fire Blossom were bought after the final kill, so neither was in any fight.
eternal: Krix raises maximum health and size; Cannibalism adds permanent max health on takedowns.
Nihil and Krix are a toss-up in the Greystone offlane field. Sound keep.
Voracity with Cannibalism is the best Krix pair; Regenerative Tissue with Cannibalism is the most played.
augment: Tainted Oath makes Sacred Oath apply Blight to enemies, a healing cut that suits facing Serath, the top enemy healer.
Imperial Soul and Tainted Oath are a toss-up in the Greystone offlane field. Sound keep.
crest: Saphir's Mantle's active briefly raises size and max health, damages nearby heroes and adds permanent max health from that damage.
Saphir's Mantle leads a toss-up in the Greystone offlane crest field. Sound keep.
improvement: Saphir's Mantle was the only item magical armor before Aegis Of Agawar; 29382 of 36580 hero damage taken was magical.
Sky Splitter's basic attacks deal a share of current health, suited to a tank like Riktor.
Draft alternative: Greystone was a second diver beside Khaimera; Kaelen tops the field's offlane swaps at 53.7%.

matchup: Duo deaths before minute ten went three to one for us against Sparrow and Argus.
Argus's Synaptic Obliterator beams slow and deal more damage the lower the target's health.
build: Dynamo is the one item built from the field's best core; Xenia and Vanguardian are missing.
Dynamo makes an immobilized enemy take more damage briefly, so a Shield Bash stun sets up the follow-up.
Flux Matrix makes nearby enemy heroes take more magical damage and cuts enemy tenacity.
eternal: Regenerative Tissue regenerates max health after 8s without hero damage; Cannibalism adds max health on each of 18 takedowns.
Idrisil, Nihil and Knell lead a toss-up in the Steel support field; Krix ranks behind all three.
augment: Heavy Metal adds bonus magical on-hit damage to Heavy Punches and Shield Bash, scaled by total armor.
Adaptive Force and Heavy Metal are a toss-up in the Steel support field. Sound keep.
crest: Sanctification's active shields Steel and nearby heroes and grants tenacity while the shield holds.
Rift Walkers and Leafsong lead a toss-up in the Steel support crest field; Sanctification, the most played, ranks behind.
improvement: No unmet need against Argus, so no item change is proven.
Rift Walkers over Sanctification stays on the Warden Crest path: a dash that pulls nearby heroes instead of the team shield.
Idrisil over Krix is the toss-up lead: bonus armor above a health threshold instead of extra max health.

matchup: Jungle opponent was Serath: Khaimera killed Serath four times and never died to Serath.
Khaimera out-earned Serath 16878 gold to 12117; Riktor scored two of four Khaimera deaths, both in our half.
build: Overlord, Sky Splitter and Draconum match the field's best core across all matchups, 63% over 92 games.
Sky Splitter shares the basic-attack trigger with Overlord, so every landed hit sets off both.
Draconum and Void Helm arrived together late, in time for the last two won fights.
eternal: Knell's Rust shreds armor on hero hits; Frequency adds attack speed per stack, and Peal maxes Rust on ultimate cast.
Lotus leans first in the Khaimera jungle field; Knell has too few games to lead.
Frequency with Peal is the best Knell pair.
augment: Jungle Invasion adds physical power in the jungle, doubled in the enemy jungle; 80 enemy-jungle minions fit that plan.
Jungle Invasion and Feral Ambush are a toss-up in the Khaimera jungle field. Sound keep.
crest: Judgement's active deals area damage around Khaimera and heals on hero hits.
Pacifier leads a toss-up in the Khaimera jungle crest field, with Eviscerator and Brutallax even; Judgement ranks right behind Eviscerator.
improvement: Core met against Serath with no unmet need; no item change is proven.
Pacifier leads Judgement but starts from Marksman Crest: a dash and empowered physical hit over the area heal.
Lotus over Knell is the field lean: random stat gains over time and on takedowns instead of armor shred.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Root a target with Static Trap, shred armor with Buckshot, stack attack speed with Hot Pursuit and finish with the long-range Charged shot or Long Arm of the Law.
ourKits.winCondition: Control space with traps and out-range enemies with Charged basic attacks, then snipe low targets anywhere with Long Arm of the Law.
ourKits.passive: Shots Fired: after 5 landed basic attacks his next one gains extra range and bonus damage.
ourKits.playWith: A frontline or peeling support, since his only escape tools are Buckshot's push back and Hot Pursuit's speed.
ourKits.playAgainst: Avoid fighting over Static Traps and engage after Buckshot is used, since it is his push-back peel. Stay out of the ult line at low health; armor does not help against Long Arm of the Law.

ourKits.combo: Hydroclasm bubble to slow, Narcosis to suspend a hero, pop the amplified bubble with Brine for extra damage and penetration, then Genesis knockup.
ourKits.winCondition: Poke with bubbles popped by Fathom and Brine, then catch a hero with Narcosis and burst them.
ourKits.passive: Herald changes his kit based on the chosen Eternal category, from damage and cooldowns to healing or anti-heal.
ourKits.playWith: Teammates with follow-up damage or CC that can hit a hero he suspends.
ourKits.playAgainst: Narcosis stops on the first hero it hits, so a tanky teammate can block it for a carry. Leave a bubble's radius before it amplifies, and fight after Narcosis is down; magical armor helps.

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap in, Make Way to shred armor, Sacred Oath empowered cleave to slow, then Stone Forged Soul to heal in Stasis and crash down.
ourKits.winCondition: Stay in the middle of fights and use Stone Forged Soul's missing-health heal to reset, while Make Way shreds armor for the team.
ourKits.passive: Stoicism deflects the next basic attack on a cooldown and grants health regen and armor that grow as he loses health.
ourKits.playWith: Damage dealers who can follow his leap and benefit from Make Way's armor shred.
ourKits.playAgainst: Do not burst into Stone Forged Soul's Stasis; step away from the slow and the crash, then re-engage. Open with an ability since Stoicism deflects a basic, and buy anti-heal to cut the ult heal.

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush in unstoppable to knock back → Shield Bash stun → Shield Slam knockup and stun, Force Shield to block projectiles
ourKits.winCondition: engage with Shield Slam or Bull Rush and protect carries with Force Shield's projectile wall
ourKits.passive: a self-shield that lasts until broken and refreshes when out of damage, plus hybrid armor
ourKits.playWith: ranged carries he can shield from enemy projectiles, and follow-up damage for his engages
ourKits.playAgainst: Bull Rush is unstoppable, so do not waste CC into it; walk around Force Shield instead of shooting into it, and fight after Shield Slam is on cooldown

ourKits.combo: Ambush leap and slow, Unleash for maximum attack speed cleaving basics, Cull to lock the target, Invigorate to cleanse and heal.
ourKits.winCondition: Stick to one target, build Rage for regen and faster cooldowns, and out-sustain them in long fights.
ourKits.passive: Ancestral Fury builds Rage on hits, giving health regen and faster cooldowns, plus movement speed at high Rage.
ourKits.playAgainst: Buy anti-heal to cut Invigorate and Rage regen. Save your CC until after Invigorate is used since it cleanses, and break off for a few seconds so his Rage decays.

enemyKits.combo: Ascend to dive onto the backline, Chastise to slow and reset her basic attack, Heaven's Fury to go untargetable and strike, then Heresy for speed, attack speed and true-damage burns.
enemyKits.winCondition: Dive the backline, get the first takedown and chain free Heresy activations from Fallen Grace.
enemyKits.passive: Fallen Grace: hero takedowns drop a visage that, when touched, activates Heresy for free and cuts her basic ability cooldowns.
enemyKits.playWith: A frontline that creates her dive angle and CC that holds targets for her.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Do not waste CC or burst during Heaven's Fury, since she is invulnerable then; hit her as she lands from Ascend. Deny the first kill so she cannot pick up the visage.

enemyKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Untamed Growth zone → Harvest Nettles stacks → Fly Trap pull and stun
enemyKits.winCondition: land Fly Trap on several heroes and follow with zone damage
enemyKits.passive: takedowns spawn an Untamed Growth and give her movement speed
enemyKits.playWith: engage that holds enemies near her Fly Trap and Bramble Patch
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has no dash, so dive her once Fly Trap is spent; stay out of Bramble Patch and Untamed Growth zones, and buy magical armor

enemyKits.combo: Riplash to pull a hero in, Shock Therapy to break their shield and silence, Electrocute aura for damage and a shield, then Skewer to suppress everyone in front of him.
enemyKits.winCondition: Land Riplash and chain silence and suppress so the target cannot fight back while their cooldowns stay frozen.
enemyKits.passive: Suspended Sentence: while his abilities immobilize or silence a hero, their cooldowns stop ticking.
enemyKits.playWith: Burst that deletes his pulled or suppressed target.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Stay behind minions or spaced so Riplash cannot reach you, and fight while it is on cooldown. Tenacity shortens the chain, which also shortens the cooldown freeze.

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses for attack speed → Hail of Arrows slow → Inner Fire barrage
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Relentless with basics and abilities to add max-health damage and melt the frontline in long fights
enemyKits.passive: Relentless stacks on hit and makes her basics deal bonus max-health damage
enemyKits.playWith: peel and a frontline, since her only escape is a short stealth
enemyKits.playAgainst: Heightened Senses is her only escape, a brief stealth with speed and no dash, so hard-engage her after it is used; Piercing Shot passes through terrain, so do not hide behind walls at low health

enemyKits.combo: Ether Crystal pushes then implodes to pull enemies together, Dread Nova stuns the group, Particle Shredder homes in, then Synaptic Obliterator beams finish low targets
enemyKits.winCondition: poke from long range, zone with Ether Crystal and land Dread Nova stuns into Obliterator beams
enemyKits.passive: abilities apply Disintegration stacks that make further ability hits deal more damage
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline to protect him while he channels Synaptic Obliterator
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Dread Nova, his only stun; dive him during the Synaptic Obliterator channel when he is immobile, and keep health high since beams hit harder on missing health; magic armor blunts his damage

loadout.name: Jungle Invasion
loadout.text: Based on Hero Level, gain 3-17 Physical Power while in the Jungle. Increases to 6-34 in the Enemy Jungle.
loadout.plain: Plain bonus physical power while you are in the jungle, doubled in the enemy jungle. It rewards invading and fighting over the other team's camps rather than any specific ability.

loadout.name: Knell
loadout.text: Attacks and abilities against Enemy Heroes apply a stack of Rust for 5s. Each stack shreds 2% (+0.2% per Level) Physical Armor and Magical Armor, stacking up to 4 times. Gain 75% of the Armors shredded.
loadout.plain: Every hit and ability strips some of the target's armor and gives it to you. Khaimera's Unleash flurry and Cull's six hits stack it fast, so you deal more and take less in extended fights.

loadout.name: Frequency
loadout.text: Gain 2% Total Attack Speed and 2 Ability Haste per Rust stack currently applied.
loadout.plain: Each armor-shred stack on a target also raises your attack speed and lowers ability cooldowns. With Unleash and basic attacks keeping stacks up, your whole rotation comes back faster.

loadout.name: Peal
loadout.text: Gain 15 Ultimate Ability Haste. Upon casting your ultimate, attacks and abilities apply maximum stacks of Rust for 4s. 20s cooldown.
loadout.plain: Lower ultimate cooldown, and casting Cull instantly applies full armor shred to everything you hit for a short while. Your post-Cull flurry lands against already-softened targets.

loadout.name: Judgement
loadout.text: Thunder Cleaver:  Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.
loadout.plain: Hit it after Ambush lands you in the middle of the enemy: it hits everyone around you and heals you per hero hit, topping you up while you wait for Invigorate.

Stack (Healing off the damage): 4 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Draconum, Void Helm, Judgement.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Overlord, Sky Splitter.
Stack (Kept alive in fights): 2 effects on one trigger: Judgement, Knell. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.

loadout.name: Jungle Invasion
loadout.text: Based on Hero Level, gain 3-17 Physical Power while in the Jungle. Increases to 6-34 in the Enemy Jungle.
loadout.plain: Plain bonus physical power while you are in the jungle, doubled in the enemy jungle. It rewards invading and fighting over the other team's camps rather than any specific ability.

loadout.name: Knell
loadout.text: Attacks and abilities against Enemy Heroes apply a stack of Rust for 5s. Each stack shreds 2% (+0.2% per Level) Physical Armor and Magical Armor, stacking up to 4 times. Gain 75% of the Armors shredded.
loadout.plain: Every hit and ability strips some of the target's armor and gives it to you. Khaimera's Unleash flurry and Cull's six hits stack it fast, so you deal more and take less in extended fights.

loadout.name: Frequency
loadout.text: Gain 2% Total Attack Speed and 2 Ability Haste per Rust stack currently applied.
loadout.plain: Each armor-shred stack on a target also raises your attack speed and lowers ability cooldowns. With Unleash and basic attacks keeping stacks up, your whole rotation comes back faster.

loadout.name: Peal
loadout.text: Gain 15 Ultimate Ability Haste. Upon casting your ultimate, attacks and abilities apply maximum stacks of Rust for 4s. 20s cooldown.
loadout.plain: Lower ultimate cooldown, and casting Cull instantly applies full armor shred to everything you hit for a short while. Your post-Cull flurry lands against already-softened targets.

loadout.name: Judgement
loadout.text: Thunder Cleaver:  Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.
loadout.plain: Hit it after Ambush lands you in the middle of the enemy: it hits everyone around you and heals you per hero hit, topping you up while you wait for Invigorate.

itemTimelineNote: estMin = first minute the role's measured median gold curve covers the cumulative inventory cost (slot order ≈ purchase order) — THEORY, no purchase timestamps in either API

fights.note: caught-out = deaths outside every clustered fight; costs/conversion use a 90s window over the per-event objective+tower stream; itemGap counts participants' items est. online (median-gold model, THEORY)

rotations.note: rotation = a laner's kill/death credited on another lane (kill location, lane radius from data/postgame tower positions; jungle/river excluded). expected = the enemy outer tower on their home lane was already down. answered = an ally died on that lane within 30s before. payoff/homeCost = our prize / our home-lane structure lost within 90s. windowsAfterOpen lists fights elsewhere after the lane opened with no kill/death credit; assists are not timestamped, so presence there is unknown. THEORY at lane edges.

evidence: 18.8m: Murdock died to Sparrow on the duo lane in our half
19.7m: Khaimera died to Riktor in our jungle
19.7m: Ikra died to The Fey in our jungle

bullets: Shield Bash and Shield Slam both stun, and each stun sets off Dynamo: the stunned enemy takes 8% more damage for 2.5s.
Flux Matrix makes nearby enemy heroes take 10% more magic damage, and Shield Bash, Bull Rush, Force Shield and Shield Slam all deal magic damage.
Forticus adds a short shield on taking hero damage, on a cooldown, beside Cybernetic Shell; Flux Matrix plus Dynamo cut Shield Slam from 95s to about 76s.
Knell's Rust stripped armor and gave Khaimera 75% of it, Peal made hits after Cull apply full Rust, and Frequency turned each stack into attack speed and haste.
Unleash's quick attacks each set off Overlord's splash and Sky Splitter's current-health damage at 65% strength, so short flurries hurt several targets at once.
Ambush leapt in, Judgement hit everyone around him and healed per hero, Draconum stacked bonus healing from the damage, and Invigorate cleansed and topped him up.

coachLean.headline: Late won fights went straight into prizes: two outer towers and Primal Fangtooth, then both inner towers, both inhibitors and the core.

flags.text: Khaimera ran the jungle: 11/4/5, 80 minions taken in their jungle and 45765 objective damage.
River buffs went 23 to 5 our way, even with their vision ahead 52 wards to 35.
Murdock died before Mini Prime; Khaimera and Ikra died after it as we lost the next fight 2-4.

focus.action: Take objectives off won fights as we did late, start Mini Prime only with all five alive, and open fights with Steel's Shield Slam chained into Khaimera's Cull.

5465c135-0f7c-423a-9fe6-8272d7d92356: Topped our hero damage with 31647 off 13010 gold, the least gold on the team.
Eight deaths against a usual 7.25, and Sparrow took 3 of them. Next game, run the pick play: Static Trap's root first, Ikra's Genesis to finish.
Farm fell to 4.9 CS a minute against a usual 6.2; clear side waves between fights to close that gap.
cf65b5c7-d458-4076-b712-271b5289b778: Killed Riktor twice, Sparrow and The Fey away from mid before it opened; one trip came with Mini Prime, another with the mid outer tower falling.
Second-most objective damage on our side at 11196, with farm up to 9.6 CS a minute.
The Fey killed him twice in the Mini Prime and Fangtooth windows; next game, hold Genesis to chain its knock-up as Khaimera's Cull ends.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Survived the game on 2 deaths with 52373 damage mitigated and 20037 healing.
Riktor got both kills on him; next game, wait out Riktor's Skewer before trading.
Hero damage ran 771 a minute against a usual 561.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Highest kill participation on the team at 58%, plus 67333 mitigated and 11167 healing.
Vision trailed: 10 wards against Argus's 24. Next game, ward Mini Prime and Fangtooth before the team calls them.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: 16 takedowns on 4 deaths with a best spree of 6, but only 3 wards placed against a usual 4.7; ward their jungle before invading.
Riktor killed him twice in mid-game fights; next game, wait out Skewer before throwing Cull.
